finding: Indian polyvalent antivenom poorly recognises E. c. sochureki from north-western India, especially SVMP classes II and III, with poor neutralisation of procoagulant activity.
note: Evaluated on every curated north-west E. c. sochureki population with a strict-majority rule (preregistration amendment A1.1).

finding: Indian polyvalent antivenom fails against the Andaman cobra Naja sagittifera; the species is phylogenetically closer to N. kaouthia than to mainland N. naja.
note: R2b substitutes N. kaouthia for N. naja in the immunogen set and requires coverage of N. sagittifera to rise by at least 0.05 absolute.

finding: Antivenoms fail against several neglected species and against the North Indian population of Bungarus caeruleus, a Big Four species.
note: R3b compares against the southern reference population nearest the Irula immunogen source (preregistration amendment A1.2).

finding: Adding more venoms to an immunising mixture can be counterproductive, diluting the antibodies specific to the toxins a given bite actually delivers.
note: Structural prediction. No population is held out for R4; the criterion is the shape of the coverage-versus-mixture-size curve and the failure of the cosine baseline to reproduce it.
